title: Brief a Plate Like a Pro
hook: Ten miles out is a terrible place to meet your approach plate.

scenes.narration: Forty miles out, ATIS says the I L S two-seven is in use, and the plate is glowing on your knee. You've got maybe three quiet minutes left, kid. Spend them right.
Three minutes of quiet. What do you brief FIRST on that plate? Commit.
onScreenText: Minimums · Missed · Top strip · Plan view

scenes.narration: Top of the plate, and work down. One: the briefing strip — frequencies, final course, runway. Two: the notes, where the fine print hides. Why top-to-bottom every time? Under stress you don't rise to the occasion, kid — you fall to your habits.
Three: plan view — the big picture. Four: the profile — final fix, step-downs, where the missed begins.
Five and six: minimums, then the missed — out loud. If you can't say the missed from memory at the fix, you briefed a bedtime story, not an approach.
Plate face-down. All six, in order. Go.
onScreenText: Say all 6 brief items, in order.

scenes.narration: Strip. Notes. Plan. Profile. Minimums. Missed. Brief it before the approach briefs you.
From the currency lesson — month thirteen with no approaches logged. What are you buying?
Instrument Procedures Handbook, chapter four. The F A A wrote four hundred pages so you'd read six.

quiz.question: A solid approach brief flows in what order?
choices: Briefing strip, notes, plan view, profile, minimums, missed
Missed approach, then plan view, then strip
Whatever order the plate prints them
quiz.explanation: Top-to-bottom keeps the brief consistent and complete — ending with minimums and the missed so they're freshest.

quiz.question: Why brief the missed approach out loud before the FAF?
choices: At minimums there's no time to read — you fly it from memory
ATC requires a readback of the missed
It's only needed for circling approaches
So your passenger can fly it
quiz.explanation: The missed happens at the busiest, lowest moment of the approach. The first steps must already be loaded in your head.
